title: Strategi Platform Governance dan Sertifikasi dalam Membangun User Trust Aset Digital
abstract: Dalam ekosistem fintech, kepercayaan digital menjadi faktor krusial bagi platform aset digital yang mengelola data sensitif dan risiko finansial tinggi. Penelitian ini menganalisis integrasi standar profesional, sertifikasi IT, dan kerangka regulasi dalam membangun arsitektur kepercayaan yang kokoh. Dengan metode kualitatif deskriptif dan analisis komparatif, studi ini membandingkan transisi pengawasan di Indonesia dari Bappebti ke Otoritas Jasa Keuangan (OJK) terhadap kerangka global seperti Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) di Uni Eropa serta regulasi di Amerika Serikat. Temuan menunjukkan kepercayaan tidak hanya bergantung pada teknologi seperti Multi-Party Computation (MPC), tetapi juga pada keselarasan Standar Kompetensi Kerja Nasional Indonesia (SKKNI) dengan standar etika internasional ACM/IEEE, serta adanya adoption gap antara laju inovasi dan kesiapan regulasi domestik.

title: Architecture Design of a Non-Custodial Web3 Wallet with Phone Number as Identifier in Indonesia Using TOGAF ADM
Phone-Number-Based Identity Abstraction for Web3 Wallets: A Systematic Literature Review
abstract: Web3 wallet adoption faces severe onboarding hurdles due to complex seed phrases and reliance on foreign social logins. Meanwhile, everyday transactions in emerging markets like Indonesia heavily rely on trusted phone number verification via SMS OTP. This study examines how this familiar habit can be leveraged as an identity abstraction method for Web3 wallets. Utilizing a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) under the PRISMA 2020 protocol, a search on Google Scholar via Publish or Perish yielded 156 initial records, narrowing down to 34 selected documents. The findings identify six primary research clusters: biometrics, social login, seed phrases, phone/SMS authentication, wallet usability, and decentralized identity theory. Crucially, existing literature shows that phone/SMS authentication remains strictly confined to conventional banking and e-government, never intersecting with Web3 wallet contexts. This separation highlights a significant research gap. The study concludes that utilizing phone numbers as an identity anchor for Web3 wallets in emerging markets presents a promising yet largely unexplored space, offering a localized, user-friendly alternative to mitigate adoption barriers.
